about: EXT-25, graded by evidence at EXT-26 by behavioural tests at EXT-27, and its runtime part again at EXT-28: what Yavin provides of the VS Code extension API, through the compatibility layer (src-tauri/crates/ide-plugin-host/src/vscode.js) and the VS Code package adapter (src-tauri/src/vsix.rs). FULL: as VS Code documents it, and tested. PARTIAL: provided with the limitation noted, and tested. STUB: present but fabricated or inert. UNSUPPORTED: fails with an UnsupportedApi error naming it (logged once). NOT VERIFIED: implemented (`implemented` says how far) but no test or benchmark run exercises its behaviour. `evidence`: L1 present (the inventory test), L2 behaviour tested, L3 exercised by real extensions in the Open VSX benchmark. 'baseline' is before EXT-25, when no VS Code extension code ran at all. Checked against the layer by crates/ide-plugin-host/tests/vscode.rs (the_inventory_matches_the_layer). EXT-27 adds L4: the window (tests/ui) and the packaged application (tests/real). EXT-29 adds the pickers, file watchers, save and selection events, formatting and code-action providers, and diagnostics in the Problems view. EXT-30 adds file icon themes (their SVG icons). EXT-31 adds webview panels.

No serializer: a panel does not survive a reload.

runtime.api: CommonJS modules (require, module.exports, relative files, JSON, node_modules)
runtime.notes: From the package's own .js, .cjs and .json files (at most 2000 files, 24 MiB). As Node.js (EXT-28): one require.cache for the extension, keyed by file name (deleting an entry loads the file again); a module whose code throws is not kept (requiring it again runs it again); circular requires see the exports as they were; module.parent, children, require, path, paths and require.main; require.resolve of a built-in is its name. An absolute path is found only inside the extension's package; climbing out of it is MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Not provided: package.json `exports` maps, require.extensions, require() of an ES module.

runtime.notes: English only ("en", "en-US"; any other locale resolves to en-US). Collator: the root collation for Latin letters, accents, case, expansions (ß, æ), digits and numeric runs, spaces, ASCII punctuation and symbols, with every option (usage, sensitivity, numeric, caseFirst, ignorePunctuation); other scripts sort by code point after Latin. localeCompare uses it, as with ICU. Segmenter: extended grapheme clusters (UAX #29); word and sentence granularity fail with UnsupportedApi. ListFormat: every type and style. DateTimeFormat: the en-US patterns of dateStyle, timeStyle and the date and time fields, in UTC and the host's own zone (named by its offset, "UTC" or such as "+05:30": no IANA names); other zones, era, dayPeriod and timeZoneName fail with UnsupportedApi. NumberFormat, PluralRules, RelativeTimeFormat, DisplayNames, Locale and DurationFormat fail with UnsupportedApi. Checked against Node.js's ICU (9 collations of 79 words, 16 texts, 23 date formats).
